description: Add a compose-based integration harness to CI (issue #272). Add a NEW job `integration` to .github/workflows/verify.yml (a separate job in the same file, so it runs on every PR alongside the existing `verify` job). The job builds and brings up `docker compose --profile full`, applies migrations from the runner against the composed DB, waits for health, runs BOTH existing smoke suites against the composed stack, runs a NEW script scripts/integration-assertions.sh that adds the ONE cross-cutting assertion the existing smoke scripts do not make (a click surviving the worker rollup from click_events into click_daily), and fails the job if any container logged an error. The other three required behaviours (real 302+Location, country-header routing, password-unlock round-trip) are ALREADY asserted by scripts/smoke-redirect.sh and are exercised for the first time against the CONTAINER images by this job. This is a CI-workflow + shell-script change only; no app/TS code changes. Cannot be validated in-sandbox (no Docker) — GitHub Actions is the arbiter. IN-WORKFLOW SECURITY RULE: never emit a command that dumps the whole environment (no env/printenv/set/export -p/process.env dump/reading /proc/self/environ); reference only the specific vars a step needs; use only the throwaway JWT values already hardcoded in docker-compose.yml.
steps: STEP 1 — New smoke assertion script. Create scripts/integration-assertions.sh (bash, `set -uo pipefail`, executable bit not required since CI invokes with `bash`). Model its ok/bad/PASSES/FAILS harness and its `dbq` DB-access helper on scripts/smoke-redirect.sh (psql on $DATABASE_URL default postgres://snapurl:snapurl@localhost:5433/snapurl, falling back to `docker exec snapurl-postgres psql -U snapurl -d snapurl`). Its job: assert that a real click lands in click_events AND survives the worker rollup into click_daily. Concretely: (a) register a workspace via API (POST $API/auth/register as smoke-redirect does), create a plain 302 link with a unique slug; (b) issue a real redirect request to $RD/<slug> and assert a 302 with a real Location header (reuse the loc() approach from smoke-redirect.sh); (c) poll click_events for a row for that link (`select count(*) from click_events where link_id in (select id from links where slug = '<slug>')`) until >=1 (bounded retry loop, e.g. 20 tries x 1s) — this proves the redirect service recorded the click; (d) then poll click_daily for that link (`select coalesce(sum(clicks),0) from click_daily where link_id in (select id from links where slug='<slug>')`) until >=1, with a generous bounded timeout (worker loop default ROLLUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS=30, so allow ~90s: 90 tries x 1s) — this proves the compose worker rolled the click up. Print clear PASS/FAIL and exit non-zero if any assertion fails. API/RD default to http://localhost:3001/api/v1 and http://localhost:3002 (overridable via env), matching the other smoke scripts. Do NOT print secrets or full env; only query the DB and the two service URLs. Add a top comment explaining this covers the rollup assertion that unit tests and the existing smoke scripts structurally cannot.

STEP 2 — New CI job. In .github/workflows/verify.yml add a second job named `integration` (name: 'Compose integration harness'), runs-on ubuntu-latest, timeout-minutes: 30, permissions contents: read (already at workflow level). Do NOT reuse the existing `services:` postgres block — the compose stack brings up its own postgres on host port 5433. Keep the existing `verify` job unchanged. GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runners already have Docker + the compose plugin, so no install step is needed.

STEP 3 — Checkout + toolchain in the new job: `actions/checkout@v4`; `pnpm/action-setup@v4` with run_install:false; `actions/setup-node@v4` with node-version 22 and cache pnpm; then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. The runner needs pnpm/node ONLY to run `pnpm db:migrate` and to have the `postgres` npm client available; the apps themselves run inside containers.

STEP 4 — Bring up the database first, migrate, then bring up the apps. Ordering rationale to encode: the composed api/redirect/worker run NODE_ENV=production and do NOT auto-migrate, and they depend_on postgres service_healthy with restart: unless-stopped (so if started against an empty schema they crash-loop until the schema exists). To guarantee the schema exists before the apps need it: (4a) `docker compose up -d --wait postgres` to start ONLY postgres and wait for its healthcheck; (4b) run migrations from the runner against the host-published DB: `DATABASE_URL=postgres://snapurl:snapurl@localhost:5433/snapurl pnpm db:migrate`; (4c) then `docker compose --profile full up -d --build --wait` to build the three images and start api/redirect/worker, waiting for the api and redirect healthchecks (the worker has no healthcheck, so `--wait` will not block on it — that is expected and correct). Set the job step names clearly (e.g. 'Start database', 'Apply migrations', 'Build and start the full stack'). If `--wait` times out, that surfaces as a failed step which the log-dump step (STEP 7) will explain.

STEP 5 — Smoke suites against the composed stack. Add steps 'Smoke — dashboard API' running `bash scripts/smoke.sh` and 'Smoke — redirect path' running `bash scripts/smoke-redirect.sh`. The composed api/redirect publish the SAME host ports (3001/3002) the scripts already target by default, and postgres is on 5433, so no env overrides are needed. smoke-redirect.sh's DB checks will use psql via $DATABASE_URL — set that env for the smoke-redirect and integration-assertions steps to postgres://snapurl:snapurl@localhost:5433/snapurl so the psql branch is taken (psql client is present on ubuntu-latest; if uncertain, the script falls back to `docker exec snapurl-postgres`). These two steps assert, against the CONTAINER images: the real 302+Location, the country-header (cloudfront-viewer-country) routing match, and the password-protected unlock round-trip.

STEP 6 — Rollup assertion step. Add a step 'Integration assertions — click rollup' running `bash scripts/integration-assertions.sh` with DATABASE_URL=postgres://snapurl:snapurl@localhost:5433/snapurl in its env. This is the click_events -> click_daily rollup assertion (the one behaviour not already covered by the smoke scripts).

STEP 7 — Log-error gate + debuggability. Add a step 'Fail on container errors' (id it so ordering is explicit; run it after the smoke + assertion steps) that greps the app containers' logs for pino error-level lines and fails if any are found. Implementation: for each app service (api, redirect, worker) run `docker compose --profile full logs --no-color <svc>` and grep for the pino error level. Match the structured pino error marker `"level":50` (pino: error=50) rather than the bare word 'error', to avoid false positives from the word 'error' appearing in a URL, a slug, or a benign info line. Collect matches; if any service has a `"level":50` line, print the offending lines and `exit 1`. Add a short comment in the workflow explaining that 50 is pino's error level and why matching the numeric level avoids false positives. Do NOT grep for/emit environment contents. (Note: the API is nestjs-pino and the redirect/worker are pino — all emit JSON with numeric `level`, so `"level":50` is the common error marker across all three.)

STEP 8 — Failure diagnostics + teardown. Add a step 'Container logs' with `if: failure()` that dumps `docker compose --profile full logs --no-color` (full, all services) and `docker compose --profile full ps` so a failed run is debuggable from the Actions log. Add a final step 'Tear down' with `if: always()` running `docker compose --profile full down -v` to remove containers and the pgdata volume. Ensure the compose commands throughout use the `--profile full` flag consistently so they address the same set of services.

STEP 9 — Review the whole verify.yml by eye: valid YAML, the `verify` job is byte-for-byte unchanged, the new `integration` job is a sibling under `jobs:`, no step dumps the environment, and only the throwaway secrets already present in docker-compose.yml are relied upon (the job sets NO JWT secrets itself — they come from docker-compose.yml for the containers, and pnpm db:migrate needs only DATABASE_URL).
acceptance_criteria: scripts/integration-assertions.sh exists, is valid bash (`bash -n scripts/integration-assertions.sh` succeeds), and asserts a click landing in click_events and surviving into click_daily via a bounded polling loop.

.github/workflows/verify.yml contains a new job `integration` alongside the unchanged `verify` job; it triggers on the same pull_request/push(main)/workflow_dispatch events (workflow-level `on:` already covers this).
The integration job brings up postgres first, runs `pnpm db:migrate` against localhost:5433 BEFORE starting the app services, then `docker compose --profile full up -d --build --wait`.
The job runs `bash scripts/smoke.sh`, `bash scripts/smoke-redirect.sh`, and `bash scripts/integration-assertions.sh` against the composed stack.
A dedicated step fails the job when any app container logs a pino error-level line (`"level":50`), and matches the numeric level (not the bare word) to avoid false positives.
A `if: failure()` step dumps full `docker compose logs` and `ps`; a `if: always()` step tears the stack down with `-v`.
No step anywhere dumps the whole environment (no env/printenv/set/export -p/process.env dump/reading /proc/self/environ), and no real secrets are introduced.
`bash -n` on both smoke scripts and the new script succeeds; `pnpm type-check` and `pnpm test` remain green (no app code changed).
verification: python3 -c "import yaml,sys; d=yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/verify.yml')); assert 'integration' in d['jobs'] and 'verify' in d['jobs']; print('jobs:', list(d['jobs']))"
findings:
Committed as 54f4a27 (feat: compose-based integration harness in CI (#272)), 2 files / 208 insertions. CHANGES: (1) NEW scripts/integration-assertions.sh — bash `set -uo pipefail`, models the ok/bad/PASSES/FAILS harness, the psql-or-`docker exec snapurl-postgres` `dbq` helper, and the `loc()` status|location parser from scripts/smoke-redirect.sh. It registers a workspace (POST $API/auth/register), creates a plain 302 link with a unique slug, issues a real redirect and asserts `302|https://example.com/rollup`, polls click_events (20 tries x 1s) for the click row, then polls click_daily via `select coalesce(sum(clicks),0) ...` (90 tries x 1s ≈ 3x the 30s worker ROLLUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS) to prove the live worker rolled it up. Defaults API=http://localhost:3001/api/v1, RD=http://localhost:3002, DB_URL=postgres://snapurl:snapurl@localhost:5433/snapurl; prints no secrets/env. (2) EDIT .github/workflows/verify.yml — appended a sibling job `integration` (name 'Compose integration harness', ubuntu-latest, timeout 30, permissions contents:read). Steps: checkout@v4, pnpm/action-setup@v4 run_install:false, setup-node@v4 node 22 cache pnpm, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; 'Start database' = `docker compose up -d --wait postgres`; 'Apply migrations' = `DATABASE_URL=... pnpm db:migrate` (only DATABASE_URL set inline, no job-level secrets); 'Build and start the full stack' = `docker compose --profile full up -d --build --wait`; 'Smoke — dashboard API' (`bash scripts/smoke.sh`); 'Smoke — redirect path' and 'Integration assertions — click rollup' both with env DATABASE_URL so the psql branch is used; a log-error gate (see below); an `if: failure()` 'Container logs' dumping `docker compose --profile full logs --no-color` + `ps`; and `if: always()` 'Tear down' = `docker compose --profile full down -v`. LOG-ERROR GREP USED: for each service in `api redirect worker`, `docker compose --profile full logs --no-color "$svc"` piped to `grep -F '"level":50'`; matches pino's numeric error level 50 (JSON fragment "level":50) rather than the bare word 'error' to avoid false positives from URLs/slugs/info lines; sets found=1 on any hit and `exit 1` at the end. ORDERING: composed api/redirect/worker run NODE_ENV=production, do NOT auto-migrate, and depend_on postgres service_healthy with restart:unless-stopped, so they crash-loop against an empty schema — the job therefore starts ONLY postgres (--wait on its healthcheck), migrates from the runner against host port 5433, THEN starts the apps; `--wait` blocks on api+redirect healthchecks but not the healthcheck-less worker (expected). The existing `verify` job is byte-for-byte unchanged (git diff origin/main = 103 insertions, 0 deletions). VERIFICATION IN-SANDBOX: `bash -n` passes on all three scripts; PyYAML parse confirms jobs=[verify, integration] and the 13 integration steps; env-dump grep found none; `pnpm type-check` and `pnpm test` both green (DB-integration/rollup vitest suites skip without a live DB, as on base). Docker/compose CANNOT run in this podman-backed sandbox, so the live compose run is validated only by GitHub Actions on the PR (per context.json).

V2 REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (addressing the 3 non-blocking findings of 2026-08-29-205246-review.md): (1) FIXED — container-error gate false positive from the worker. The 'Fail on container errors' step (id log_error_gate) now greps only `api redirect` (dropped `worker` from the loop). Rationale added in the step comment: the issue's target is a silently-broken ADAPTER (api/redirect serving wrong-but-2xx); the worker legitimately logs at pino error level 50 for benign operational conditions (a stuck projection in runMaintenance, and everyN's `job failed` on any caught exception in apps/worker/src/jobs/rollup.ts and apps/worker/src/main.ts), which would false-positive and flake the run. Still matches the numeric `"level":50` marker, not the bare word. The `if: failure()` 'Container logs' step is UNCHANGED and still dumps `docker compose --profile full logs` for ALL services (plus `ps`), so a worker crash remains diagnosable; a dead worker also independently fails the rollup assertion. (2) NO CODE CHANGE (confirmed intentional) — the worker has no healthcheck so `docker compose --profile full up --wait` returns before the worker is proven up. This is acceptable and by design: the rollup assertion in scripts/integration-assertions.sh polls click_daily for ~90s and fails if the worker never rolls the click up, backstopping a dead/crash-looping worker. The failure mode is a slow ~90s timeout rather than a fast healthcheck failure, which is an accepted trade-off (the worker serves no HTTP, so a healthcheck would be synthetic). (3) HARDENED (comment only, no behavioural change) — added a comment in scripts/integration-assertions.sh at the click_daily poll loop noting the 90s budget assumes the compose worker's default ~30s ROLLUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS (docker-compose.yml sets no override today) and that the poll count must be raised (~3x the interval) if that override is ever increased, so config drift is not mistaken for a rollup bug. RE-VERIFIED in-sandbox: `bash -n scripts/integration-assertions.sh` passes; PyYAML parse confirms jobs==[verify, integration]; env-dump grep (printenv|export -p|process.env|/proc/self/environ|bare env|set -x) found none; the gate loop is now `for svc in api redirect`; `pnpm type-check` and `pnpm test` both green (same DB suites skip as on base). The `verify` job remains byte-for-byte unchanged. No app/TS code touched.
